title: NDA (Defence)
kicker: Government / Competitive · Armed forces officer entry

value.body: The National Defence Academy (NDA) at Khadakwasla, Pune trains future officers of the Army, Navy and Air Force. Cadets complete a 3-year joint course that includes a degree, then about a year at their own service academy, before being commissioned as officers. The NDA & NA exam, held by UPSC, is one of the few officer routes open straight after Class 12.

items.label: Vacancies per exam
items.note: 406 in NDA & NA (I) 2025, including the Naval Academy

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 or equivalent — any stream for the Army wing, and Physics and Mathematics for the Air Force, Navy and Naval Academy; Class 12 students can apply while awaiting results. Selection: a UPSC written exam (Mathematics and a General Ability Test), then a multi-day SSB interview, then a medical examination.

value.title: At a glance
items: Strict physical and medical standards apply, including eyesight; it helps to check them before preparing.
Clearing the written exam is only the first step — the SSB interview has its own separate assessment.
It is a long-term commitment: officers serve under a service contract with the armed forces.
Later routes also exist: the 10+2 Technical Entry Scheme (Army) for PCM students, and CDS after graduation.
